TrinaTracker ships first Buildex installation robots to Europe

The shipment serves a Portuguese solar project, with ESI Robotics supporting integration and commissioning.

TrinaTracker / pv magazine ↗28 October 2026English editorial summary
Story

A shipment for Portugal

TrinaTracker announced its first European shipment of Buildex module-installation robots for a Portuguese solar project. ESI Robotics will support integration, commissioning and engineering. Shipment is a new milestone, not evidence of sustained operating results at this project.

Leveling and module handling

Buildex provides automatic angular adjustment up to 17 degrees and supports fixed-tilt structures and TrinaTracker’s 1P and 2P tracking systems. Multi-source vision identifies installation positions, flexible suction grips modules, and lidar with AI sensing detects people and obstacles.

Company-reported field results

TrinaTracker cites 600–700 modules per day, three to four times manual productivity, 22.2% lower module-installation costs and 17.5% shorter project installation time. These are reported field-test figures, not independently certified outcomes or established results for every condition at the Portuguese site.
